# Read QC and Preprocessing

Domain knowledge for short-read quality control, trimming, and
read-level filtering tasks.

## Expected Workflow

1. Check the input facts first:
   - single-end or paired-end
   - read length
   - expected adapters or library type
   - whether the task is trimming, contamination removal, or both
2. Choose the lightest preprocessing that solves the actual problem.
3. Verify that quality improves after trimming instead of assuming it did.
4. If reads are being removed against a reference, define exactly what
   “retained” means before running the filter.
5. Accept the branch only if the outputs and reports describe the same
   retained-read definition.

## Quality Control and Trimming

- **Purpose**: Remove low-quality bases, adapter sequences, and reads that

2026-08-27 paired-end QC and trimming

Inputs
- R1: data/inputs/raw_reads/pair/forward/forward.fastqsanger.gz (MD5 8465881bfa357710b09137b902eeb141)
- R2: data/inputs/raw_reads/pair/reverse/reverse.fastqsanger.gz (MD5 2f14284d27d0d9210b825e38bb6df5d9)
- Input records: 377961 synchronized pairs

Execution
- Tool: fastp 1.3.6
- Adapter handling: paired-read overlap trimming only; no adapter sequence and no --detect_adapter_for_pe
- Filters: Q < 20 is low quality; reject pair if either mate has >40% low-quality bases, >5 Ns, or post-adapter length <15
- Disabled/non-enabled operations: poly-G trimming disabled; no poly-X, fixed-end, sliding-window, or quality-end trimming; no base correction
- Command: /tmp/fastp.1.3.6 --in1 data/inputs/raw_reads/pair/forward/forward.fastqsanger.gz --in2 data/inputs/raw_reads/pair/reverse/reverse.fastqsanger.gz --out1 final_answer/trimmed_forward.fastqsanger.gz --out2 final_answer/trimmed_reverse.fastqsanger.gz --qualified_quality_phred 20 --unqualified_p
